chunks: Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Zurārah, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام concerning a man who killed in the Sanctuary:
He said: “Upon him is the blood money and one-third extra, and he must fast two consecutive months from the sacred months.”
He said: I said, “This includes the ʿĪd and the days of Tashrīq.”
He said: So he said, “He fasts, for it is an obligation that has become binding upon him.”

key_terms.أَشْهُرِ الْحُرُمِ: the sacred months in which certain violations are treated with added seriousness
key_terms.أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ: the days following ʿĪd al-Aḍḥā referred to in the question
key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: the sacred sanctuary in which violation carries a heightened legal consequence
key_terms.ثُلُثٌ: an additional one-third added to the diyyah as an aggravated penalty
key_terms.حَقٌّ لَزِمَهُ: a binding obligation that has become incumbent upon him
key_terms.دِيَةٌ: blood money owed for unlawful killing
key_terms.شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ: two consecutive months of fasting without interruption

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who kills in the Haram according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who kills within the sacred sanctuary: an aggravated diyyah is due, along with fasting two consecutive months in the sacred months. It further clarifies that this binding expiation is to be observed even when it coincides with ʿĪd and the days of Tashrīq, emphasizing the gravity of violating the sanctity of the Haram.
